cells.remarks: The plate belongs to the Trustee of the Kailāsanātha temple at Molaiyur, Kumbakonam taluk. The characters are too modern and it is dated in the names of certain Vijayanagara kings are given without any order. Purports to register an agreement made among the residents of several villages of the Pandanallūr-śīrmai to pay imposts at certain rates per head-load on grains and other articles of merchandise, for providing for the daily offerings and worship in the temple of Kailāsanāthasvāmi and Saundaryamman at Muḷaiyūr. Records the agreement given to the temple authorities by the Karṇams, Śeṭṭis and the Reḍḍis (phanams of the several villages (in his estate), settling in cash the amount of annual rent to be paid by each village on its tobacco crops.

cells.remarks: Refers to the chief as the son of Immaḍi Chikkaryā and Dēvī-rammaṇi (the daughter of Timmayya-Rājayagāṇivāru) and the grandson of Mummadi Chikkaryā of the Sadāśiva-gōtra. Registers an endowment of lands, made by the chief for the daily and special worships, offerings and lamps in the temple of Śiva built by him near Bhīmapuram attached to the Mōḍugulapalle-sthala, and also the construction of a tank by him in the same place. Registers also the chief's renovation of the village-tank to the south of the temple, and his foundation of a garden near its borders. Records a supplementary gift of land made by the chief in Dhātu, on Āśvija, śu. 10, to the same temple.

cells.location: Anḍār
cells.place: On the north wall of the Vēdanāyāna-Perumāḷ tem- ple.
cells.remarks: Fragmentary. Seems to register some provision made for worship and midnight offerings in the temple of Dēvēndratu... by the assembly (sabhā) of the village. Mentions Kalattūr-nāḍu in [Kala]ttūr-kōṭṭam. Forms part of a gift of gold by the Mahā- sabhā of Āṇḍūr in Kalattūr-kōṭṭam as bhaṭṭavṛitti to a brāhmaṇa (name lost) of the village, well-versed in one Vēda besides the Sāma-Vēda, in the Pāṇini grammar, in the Mīmāṁsā, etc., without detriment to the money- payments for the temple lamps. It seems to mention Tiruttaṇi, to which this land had originally been assign- ed. The donee was to teach subjects to four pupils and feed them daily. There are three more frag- ments, one of which seems to record provision made for playing musical instruments during the service in the temple; another is a part of a record of Pārthivēndravarman[rman] and the third, of Rājarāja I. States that the temple of Chittiramēḷi-Viṇṇagar in the village of Āṇḍūr in Kalattūr-kōṭṭam in the Pariya-Nāḍu- maṇḍalam was the gift of the Pariya-Nāḍavar (district assembly). The characters belong to the 13th century A.D.

cells.remarks: Stones misplaced and portions lost. cells.location: Tirukkalukkunram
cells.place: cont.
cells.king: Tribhuvanaviradēva, ‘who taken Madura, Īḷam, Karuvūr and the crowned head of the Pāṇḍya,’ who was pleased to take the anointment of heroes and of victors’.
cells.remarks: Stones misplaced and lost. Two of the three stones containing this inscription are built into the west wall of the same prākāra. States that a certain Poriyāṉ, handed with the temple, having been charged with theft of the gold ornaments of the deity stolen by him, he was ejected as a drōhin from his house in the western street (of the maḍavilāgam), which was then confiscated and sold to Talaikkāvviri Pālarāvaṉaṉ a-vīraṇār, an agent of the assembly (the 100-pillared maṇḍapa of the temple), and the proceeds were utilized for paying the masons and other workmen employed in the construction of the steps to the 100-pillared maṇḍapa in the third prākāra of the temple.

Sōmana-Peggaḍa was the daṇḍanātha of Magaḍala of the Durjaya family.

cells.location: Meḍikoṇḍuru

cells.remarks: Registers the grant of visama-income made to the god Prasanna-Gōpinātha, by the Kāpus and the Eighteen Communities of the village Meḍikoṇḍuru, for the merit of the king. Records that the tank called Kummari-cheruvu was constructed by his wife Prōlāmbikā was also called after the king's name as Prōlāmbikā-samudra. Komma, the son of Chōḍa (i.e., Rājēndra-Chōḍa) Komma is stated to have built the temple of Kunārēśvara and constructed the tank called Dāmaranāyapaḍu. Registers the grant of lands made for the offerings of the god, and to the Brahmans, and the gift of 55 sheep for a perpetual lamp to the god Sōmēśvaradēva of the village, by the same minister who is called also Maṇḍadi Kommanāyaka who is styled the 'lord of the town of Oṅgōru'.

cells.location: Jammalamadugu †

Records the gift of 4½ varāhas of Dommaripannu realized from the village of Kōḍūru on the bank of (the river) Penna, for the maintenance of the lamps of the Dommari caste, for the offerings and lamps of the god Chennakēśava of the village. Refers to the village [Kōḍūru] on the bank of the river Penna in the Guṭṭi-sīma.

cells.location: Śivagaṅga (near Masulipatam)
cells.place: On the left side of the entrance into the garbhagṛiha of the Mahishāsuramardini temple.
cells.remarks: Registers the consecration of the images of the god Vidyāśatīkarēśvara and the goddess Nāgarīpurī Durgā-Bhavānī, the family deity of the Dēvarakōṭa chiefs, on the bank of the Śivagaṅga (tank), by Rāja Yērlagaḍḍa Aṅkinēḍu-Bahadaru, for the private worship of the chiefs (of the family). The ceremony was performed by Abhinavōddaṇḍa Śaṅkara-Bhārathīsvāmin. Records the names of the devotees (of the above-mentioned goddess) Yōrlagaḍḍa Nāgēśvara-Nāyaka and (his two wives) Satyaprasītamāmbā and Rājyalakshmī. Standing figures of the chief and his two wives also carved here with hands raised in obeisance. This is a copy of No. 401 above.

cells.remarks: States that Mahāpradhāna Dāsirāja constructed the temple of Sōmēśvara-pura and endowed it with land, after purchasing it from the king. Records a gift of the village Koḍaḷiya Haḷḷi, by the king, after its purchase from Dāsirāja, to Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Mācharasa to Rōyaguru Kalyāṇa-śaktidēva. Also registers a gift of the village Koṇṇavāḍi in Noḷambavāḍi, made to the same temple by Dāsirāja, after its purchase from Dāsirāja, on the occasion of his coronation. Also registers a gift of the village (name lost) made by Sōmaladēvi, Dēvarasa, etc., on the occasion of the coronation of, Vijaya-Pāṇḍyadēva, son of Oḍeyarasadēva. The recipient of the gifts was Kalyāṇaśaktidēva.

cells.date: (1) Śaka 1104 (in words) Śivaratri, Utta-rāyaṇa-saṅkrānti. (2) Śaka 1110, Plavaṅga, Phālguṇa, śu. 13, Thursday.
cells.remarks: Portions damaged. States that Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Jōyidēva constructed, at the instance of Kalyāṇaśakti-dēva, the temple of Sōmēśvara on the bank of the river Tuṅgabhadrā, and the temple of the god Svayambhu-Guṭṭēśvara (in the vicinity of the temple of Svayambhu-Bhu-Sōmanāthadēva therein. Registers a gift of the village Goṭṭagaḍi and another (name lost) in Haḷeyanāḍu, made to the temple, after obtaining a copper-plate charter for the temple, Ballaha (i.e., the king) through Maḷugi-Daṇḍanāyaka. Also records a gift of land and taxes made by Vira-Vikramāditya and Mahāpradhāna Sōmanāthadēva to the aforementioned, and the temple of the god. The recipient of the gifts was Kalyāṇaśakti of the Kāḷāmukha sēct.

cells.location: Hāvēri †

cells.date: 8th year, Puṣya, ba. 3, Monday, Vyatīpāta, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Traces the king's genealogy from Taila II. States that Heggaḍe Rudradēva, the son of Mādirāja, an officer (maḍaladēva) of the village Kisuvaḍi in Kinakuḍu Seventy, was a subordinate of Kēśirāja, the governor of Doṇi-nāḍu, and that he who was a feudatory of Mahārājādhirāja Bhujabalachakravartin Kala-huryya Bijjaḷadēva. Registers a gift of annual money-income made by Rudradēva and other karaṇas, for the benefit of the tank Hiriya-kere constructed by Nēra-dēva. Mentions that the village was a gift of taxes made by Sunkadaveggaḍe Ratnabhaṭṭa-Dēva of Hāyaka, for the same tank and to the temples of Siddheśvara and Indrēśvara of the place.

cells.remarks: Slightly mutilated. cells.location: Mallūr †
cells.place: Another slab standing in the place of Kaḷamēśvara. †
cells.remarks: Slightly damaged. Registers a gift of land and house-sites made to the temple of Kalāmanēra at Mallavura by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kumāra Jōmadēvarasa, on the occasion of the Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti. He was also the Jīmūtavāhana lineage who was administering Bāsavura One Hundred and Forty. Jōmadēvarasa is stated to be the son of Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Barmmadēvarasa and grandson of Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Chāvuṇḍarāyasa, who was governing Bāsavura One Hundred and Forty at the time of the grant.

cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land made to the temple of Pārśvanā-thasvāmi of Saṅgūr by Nēmanaya, son of Saṅgāma-dēva and grandson of Jaina-Mallappa, who was the son of Gōpa and grandson of Jaina-Mallappa and who obtained from the village Chāvuṇḍa-rāya, who was the minister of king Harihara, son of Bukkarāja, at Vijayanagara. The gift was made for conducting worship to the tombs of his ancestors who died. The ancestors were: his father, Mallappa-nāyaka, who died at Guṭṭi in Naḷa, Phālguṇa, ba. 14 Monday, and his son Saṅgāma drowned himself in the sea in Śaka 1317, Yuva, Pushya, śu. 11, Thursday.

cells.location: Sahgūr †
cells.place: Slab standing in the temple of Virabhadra. †
cells.remarks: Damaged. Seems to register a gift of land made by Mahāpradhāna Herggade Bommarasa, the governor of Banavāsi Twelve Thousand, to the god Brahmēśvara-dēva, when Kalyāṇamādēva was the Jimūtavāhana lineage and the Khachara race was governing the province. The gift was entrusted to Brahmariāhi-Paṇḍita, son of Kalidēva-Paṇḍita and the āchārya of the temple of Brahmēśvara. Also records gifts of land and tax made by Daṇṇāyaka Tippa.
